all_quotes.loc: The CN/HCN intensity ratio as a probe of radiation field
all_quotes.quote: The intensity ratio of CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) $\sim1.7$ in the northern nucleus of NGC 3256 is reproduced with N~CN~/N~HCN~ $\sim24$.
The HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) intensity ratio varies in NGC 3256 and NGC 7469, with superlinear trends of $1.53\pm0.07$ and $1.55\pm0.05$, respectively.
At our resolution ($\sim700$ pc), IRAS 13120-5453 shows little variation in the HCN intensity ratios.

We find relatively constant CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) ratios and subtle variations in the CN (3-2)/CN (2-1) ratio in our galaxy sample. We find an offset to lower ratios of $\sim0.45$ in the CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) ratio in NGC 3256 compared to $\sim0.8$ in NGC 7469 and IRAS 13120.

We find high ($\sim1.7$) CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) intensity ratios in IRAS 13120-5453 and in the northern nucleus of NGC 3256, compared to a more constant ratio ($\sim1.1$) in NGC 7469 and non-starbursting regions of NGC 3256.

The HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) ratio in NGC 7469 shows the largest difference between non-nuclear ($0.33\pm0.04$) and nuclear ($0.52\pm0.06$) regions. We attribute the regions of enhanced HCN excitation in NGC 7469 to the central AGN, where both an XDR and shocks in outflows can heat the gas and increase HCN excitation.
The HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) ratio in IRAS 13120 is higher ($\sim0.8$) than both NGC 3256 ($\sim0.27-0.39$) and NGC 7469 ($\sim0.33-0.52$).

Individual galaxies show nearly constant CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) intensity ratios. We find an offset to lower CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) intensity ratios ($\sim0.5$) in NGC 3256 compared to the other two galaxies ($\sim0.8$).
For the CN (3-2)/CN (2-1) intensity ratio, NGC 7469 has a superlinear trend of $1.55\pm0.04$, with the peak localized toward the active galactic nucleus.

The CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) ratio is higher ($1.7$) in the northern nucleus of NGC 3256 than in the rest of the galaxy. We find a similarly high CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) ratio in the starburst galaxy IRAS 13120.

The CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) ratio in NGC 7469 is $\sim1.1$ and is relatively constant across the entire galaxy. NGC 7469 is dominated by a nuclear AGN, which does not appear to affect the CN/HCN ratio as significantly as the starbursts in the other galaxies.

In this paper, we present the results of an observational study of the intensity ratios of CN and HCN in three U/LIRGs. We use both new and archival ALMA observations of three lines each of CN and HCN. The higher energy lines allow us to explore the interaction between these molecules in a variety of radiation environments.
The different galaxy environments available in this sample allow us to probe the effects of both UV and X-ray radiation fields on the molecular gas.
The UVRANGE parameter was matched between all lines in each galaxy in order to recover similar flux scales for each line.
An RMS cut-off of $3.5\sigma$ was used to mask the cleaned cubes to include strong emission while avoiding noisy emission in lines with lower S/N.

We used the Linmix linear regression method to fit the integrated intensity pixels in log-log space and account for the higher uncertainties seen in the lower S/N pixels (cite: Kelly2007; Meyers2018).

We performed the same analysis applying a conservative estimate for inclination angles of $60^\circ$ to NGC 3256 and IRAS 1320 and found that the resulting slopes and intercepts match the results in Table 5 within one standard deviation.

We note that applying a *uv* cut-off and taper with the UVRANGE and UVTAPER parameters in TCLEAN will limit the number of short baselines in our data and thus could potentially lead to missing flux on the largest angular scales.

all_quotes.loc: Increased nuclear HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) ratio in NGC 7469
all_quotes.quote: Our observations of NGC 7469 have a resolution of $\sim300$ pc and thus blend the influence of both AGN and starburst activity in the circumnuclear disk.

all_quotes.loc: Higher HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) ratios in IRAS 13120 than NGC 3256
all_quotes.quote: Our resolution of $\sim700$ pc is insufficient to isolate the nuclear region and so the line ratio will have contributions from both the starburst and AGN components in this galaxy.

The CN (1-0) data for NGC 3256 is our only data set from ALMA Cycle 0. As such, the flux measurements and intensity ratios using this line in this galaxy have the highest calibration uncertainties of our sample. Given the similarity of the slopes in the CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) ratio of all three galaxies, the offset in the ratio in NGC 3256 could be due to large observational uncertainties.
We note that opacity effects could potentially be important and determining the CN/HCN abundance ratios is the next step in this analysis.
